title: The car, the house: the definite form
description: Say the in Swedish with an ending on the noun, in the singular and plural, with adjectives and after my.

guide.summary: Swedish puts the at the end of the noun: bil, bilen; hus, huset. Learn the endings, the plural, the double marking with adjectives and when the ending is left out, and you can point at anything.

sections.title: The: an ending on en-words
sections.text: Swedish has no separate word for the. Instead the noun gets an ending. En-words add -en, or just -n when the noun already ends in a vowel.
steps: Check that the noun is an en-word.
Drop the word en.
Ends in a consonant? Add -en. Ends in a vowel? Add only -n.
watch: Never keep en and the ending together: en bilen is wrong.
Den is not the word for the in front of a lone noun: den bil is wrong.

sections.title: The: an ending on ett-words
sections.text: Ett-words do the same with a t: -et, or just -t after a vowel.
steps: Check that the noun is an ett-word.
Drop the word ett.
Ends in a consonant? Add -et. Ends in a vowel? Add only -t.

examples.en: The child is sleeping in the bedroom.

watch: A short vowel before a final m doubles the m: rum, rummet; hem, hemmet.
Do not confuse huset (the house) with husen (the houses).

sections.title: Nouns ending in -el and -er
sections.text: Many nouns that end in an unstressed -el or -er do not add a second e. En-words just add -n; ett-words drop the e and add -et.
steps: Does the noun end in unstressed -el or -er?
For an en-word, add only -n.
For an ett-word, drop that e and add -et.
watch: Fågelen and systeren are not written.
The e stays in the singular definite: cykeln, not cyklen. It drops only in the plural: cyklar.

sections.title: The definite plural
sections.text: Make the plural first, then add the definite plural ending. Plurals in -ar, -or, -er or a vowel add -na. Ett-words with no plural ending add -en. Plurals ending in -n add -a.
steps: Find the plural of the noun.
Plural ends in -r or a vowel? Add -na.
Plural is the same as the singular? Add -en.
Plural ends in -n? Add -a.

examples.en: The cars are parked in the street.
The children are eating the apples.

watch: Husena and barnena are wrong: plurals with no ending take -en.
Do not build from the singular: the girls is flickorna, not flickarna.

sections.title: The with an adjective
sections.text: When an adjective comes before a definite noun, Swedish marks the twice: a front word den, det or de, the adjective in -a, and the noun with its ending.
steps: Pick the front word: den for en-words, det for ett-words, de for plurals.
Give the adjective the ending -a.
Keep the definite ending on the noun.
watch: Den stora bil is wrong: the noun keeps its ending.
Without an adjective there is no front word: bilen, not den bilen, for the car.
In everyday speech the front word is often dropped: nya bilen, stora huset. In writing keep it.

sections.title: After my, your and a genitive
sections.text: A possessive like min, din, mitt or a genitive like Annas already says which thing, so the noun stays bare, with no ending.
steps: Is there a possessive or a genitive with -s before the noun?
If yes, use the bare noun with no ending.
If no and you mean the, add the ending.
watch: Min bilen is the most common slip: drop the ending.
Mitt goes with ett-words: mitt hus.

sections.title: When to use the definite form
sections.text: Use the definite form where English says the about a known thing. For things in general, Swedish like English uses the bare plural or the bare noun.
steps: Does English say the about a particular thing? Use the ending.
Is it a general statement with no the? Leave the noun bare.

examples.en: The dogs in the garden are big.

watch: Food and drink as a habit stay bare: Jag dricker kaffe.
Some abstract nouns take the ending where English has none: Livet är kort means Life is short.

steps: Check that the noun is an en-word.
Ends in a consonant? Add -en.
Ends in a vowel? Add only -n.
Check that the noun is an ett-word.
Ends in a consonant? Add -et.
Ends in a vowel? Add only -t.
Look for an unstressed -el, -er or -en at the end.
En-word: add only -n.
Ett-word: drop the e and add -et.
Make the plural.
Plural in -r or a vowel: add -na.
Plural same as singular: add -en; plural in -n: add -a.
Choose den, det or de by the noun.
Put the adjective in -a.
Keep the ending on the noun.
Look for min, din, mitt or a name with -s before the noun.
If there is one, leave the noun bare.
Ask whether English uses the for a particular thing.
Particular: add the ending. General: leave the noun bare.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the car.
exercises.hint: Bil is an en-word. Where does the word for the go?
exercises.feedback: In Swedish, the is an ending glued to the noun.
exercises.explanation: Bil is an en-word ending in a consonant, so the car is bilen: bil + -en.

mistakes.why: The ending -et belongs to ett-words. Bil is an en-word (en bil), so it takes the en ending.
That is the bare noun, a car or car in general. The question asks for one particular car, so the noun needs its definite ending.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the girl.
exercises.hint: Flicka already ends in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: After a vowel the en ending shrinks to one letter.
exercises.explanation: Flicka ends in -a, so only -n is added: flickan.

mistakes.why: Swedish does not stack a vowel on a vowel here: after a final -a the ending loses its e.
Without an ending this is just girl, with no the. The sentence is about one known girl.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite form: the door.
exercises.hint: Dörr is an en-word ending in a consonant.
exercises.feedback: Glue the en ending onto dörr.
exercises.explanation: Dörr is an en-word (en dörr) ending in r, so the door is dörren.

mistakes.why: That is the noun without its ending, so it means door, not the door.
The -et ending is for ett-words, and dörr is an en-word.
Swedish has no separate word for the in front of a plain noun; the meaning lives in an ending.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite form: the lamp.
exercises.hint: Lampa ends in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: After a final vowel, add only one letter.
exercises.explanation: Lampa is an en-word ending in -a, so it takes just -n: lampan.

mistakes.why: After a vowel the ending drops its e; Swedish does not write -aen.
That is lamp with no the. The sentence talks about one known lamp.
The -a of lampa stays; the ending is added after it, not in its place.

exercises.instruction: Make buss definite: the bus. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Drop en and add the ending.
exercises.feedback: The indefinite article goes and the ending comes in.
exercises.explanation: The bus is bussen: en disappears and -en is glued to buss.

mistakes.why: A noun is either indefinite (en buss) or definite (with the ending), never both at once.
Removing en is not enough; the noun still needs its ending to mean the bus.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.hint: Pojke ends in a vowel; buss does not.
exercises.feedback: Both nouns are definite, so both get an ending.
exercises.explanation: Pojke ends in -e, so it adds -n: pojken. Buss adds -en: bussen.

mistakes.why: After a final vowel the ending is only -n.
Without endings the nouns lose the; Swedish shows the only through the ending.
Den is not the Swedish the in front of a lone noun. Use the ending instead.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the house.
exercises.hint: Hus is an ett-word. Is the subject one house or several?
exercises.feedback: Ett-words take a t ending.
exercises.explanation: Hus is an ett-word (ett hus) ending in a consonant, so the house is huset.

mistakes.why: Husen means the houses, plural. Stort describes one house.
That is house with no the, and the sentence speaks about a known house.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the apple.
exercises.hint: Äpple ends in a vowel.
exercises.feedback: After a vowel the ett ending is just -t.
exercises.explanation: Äpple is an ett-word ending in -e, so only -t is added: äpplet.

mistakes.why: Äpplen is the plural, apples. You are eating one particular apple.
After a final vowel the ending loses its e, so Swedish never writes -eet here.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite form: the table.
exercises.hint: Bord is an ett-word.
exercises.feedback: Ett-words ending in a consonant take -et.
exercises.explanation: Bord is ett bord, so the table is bordet.

mistakes.why: Borden means the tables. Rent is the form for one ett-word, and the sentence names one table.
Without its ending the noun means table, not the table.
Bord ends in a consonant, so its ending is the ett ending, not -een.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.hint: Look at the ending after the final vowel of äpple.
exercises.feedback: After a vowel the ett ending is a single letter.
exercises.explanation: Äpple already ends in -e, so the apple is äpplet, with -t only.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: after the final -e the ending should not repeat the e.
Äpplen means apples. The sentence takes one apple, so only the ending needs fixing.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: The train is at the station. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.source: The train is at the station.
exercises.hint: Tåg is an ett-word.
exercises.feedback: One tile is a plural form.
exercises.explanation: Tåg is ett tåg, so the train is tåget; station is an en-word, so the station is stationen.

mistakes.why: Tågen means the trains. The English talks about one train.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: The child is sleeping in the bedroom.
exercises.hint: Barn and sovrum are both ett-words. Rum doubles its m.
exercises.feedback: Both nouns take the ett ending.
exercises.explanation: Ett barn becomes barnet. Ett sovrum becomes sovrummet: a short vowel before m doubles the m.

mistakes.why: Rum has a short vowel, so the m doubles before the ending: rummet.
Barnen means the children. The English has one child.
Sovrummen is plural; the child sleeps in one bedroom.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the bird.
exercises.hint: Fågel ends in -el.
exercises.feedback: Nouns in -el just add -n.
exercises.explanation: Fågel ends in -el, so the e does not repeat: fågeln.

mistakes.why: Nouns ending in unstressed -el take only -n; -elen is not written.
The e of -el stays in the singular. It drops only in the plural, fåglar.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the bike.
exercises.hint: Cykel ends in -el, like fågel.
exercises.feedback: The ending for these nouns is a single -n.
exercises.explanation: Cykel ends in -el, so the bike is cykeln.

mistakes.why: After -el the ending is only -n, never -en.
The singular keeps the e: cykel, cykeln. Cyklar is the plural.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite form: the key.
exercises.hint: Nyckel ends in -el.
exercises.feedback: Just add -n.
exercises.explanation: Nyckel ends in -el, so the key is nyckeln.

mistakes.why: Nouns in -el take only -n; the extra e is wrong.
That is key with no the. You are asking about one known key.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite form: the window.
exercises.hint: Fönster is an ett-word in -er.
exercises.feedback: The e before r drops when the ending comes.
exercises.explanation: Fönster is ett fönster. The e of -er drops and -et is added: fönstret.

mistakes.why: Ett-words in -er lose that e before the ending, so -eret is not written.
Fönstren means the windows, plural. You are opening one window.
Fönster is an ett-word, so it takes the ett ending, not -n.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.hint: Syster ends in -er and is an en-word.
exercises.feedback: En-words in -er just add -n.
exercises.explanation: Syster is en syster. It ends in -er, so the sister is systern.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: -er nouns do not take -en.
Without the ending the noun means sister, not the sister.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: The mirror is in the bathroom.
exercises.hint: Spegel ends in -el; badrum doubles its m.
exercises.feedback: Two definite nouns, two endings.
exercises.explanation: Spegel ends in -el, so it adds -n: spegeln. Ett badrum becomes badrummet.

mistakes.why: After -el the ending is only -n.
Rum doubles its m before the ending.
Badrummen means the bathrooms, plural.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the cars.
exercises.hint: Start from the plural bilar.
exercises.feedback: The definite plural adds -na to the plural.
exercises.explanation: The plural of bil is bilar, and the cars is bilar + na: bilarna.

mistakes.why: Bilar means cars, any cars. The sentence points at known cars, so it needs -na.
Bilen is the car, one car. The question asks for several.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the apples.
exercises.hint: The plural äpplen already ends in -n.
exercises.feedback: Ett-words with a plural in -n add -a.
exercises.explanation: Äpple has the plural äpplen, so the apples is äpplena.

mistakes.why: Äpplen means apples in general, without the.
Äpplet is the apple, only one.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite plural: the houses.
exercises.hint: Hus has the same form in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Ett-words ending in a consonant take -en in the definite plural.
exercises.explanation: The plural of hus is hus, and the houses is husen.

mistakes.why: -na goes only after a plural that ends in a vowel or -n like äpplen. Hus takes -en.
Hus does not have an -ar plural; it stays hus, so the houses is formed from that.
Huset is the house, one house, and gamla is plural.

exercises.instruction: Write the definite plural: the shoes.
exercises.hint: Skor is the plural. Add the definite plural ending.
exercises.feedback: Plurals ending in -r take -na.
exercises.explanation: Skor ends in -r, so the shoes is skorna.

mistakes.why: That is shoes with no the. You mean particular shoes.
Skon is the shoe, just one.
Plurals in -r take -na, not -en.

exercises.instruction: Make flickan plural: the girls. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: The plural of flicka is flickor.
exercises.feedback: Plural first, then -na.
exercises.explanation: Flicka has the plural flickor, so the girls is flickorna. The verb does not change.

mistakes.why: Flicka makes its plural with -or, so the -ar form does not exist.
Flickor means girls, without the.
That is the original sentence, still one girl.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: The children are eating the apples. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.source: The children are eating the apples.
exercises.hint: Barn is the same in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Barn takes -en, äpplen takes -a.
exercises.explanation: The children is barnen, and the apples is äpplena.

mistakes.why: Barn ends in a consonant, so its definite plural is -en, not -ena.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: The keys are on the table.
exercises.hint: Nyckel has the plural nycklar.
exercises.feedback: Plural first, then -na.
exercises.explanation: Nyckel has the plural nycklar, so the keys is nycklarna. Swedish often says ligger, lie, for things on a table.

mistakes.why: Nycklar means keys in general, with no the.
In the plural nyckel drops its e: nycklar.
The table is a known table too, so bord needs its ending.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word that starts the phrase the big car.
exercises.hint: Bil is an en-word.
exercises.feedback: With an adjective the needs an extra word in front.
exercises.explanation: Bil is an en-word, so the big car is den stora bilen.

mistakes.why: Det goes with ett-words. Bil is an en-word.
De is for plurals, and bilen is one car.

exercises.instruction: Choose the missing word.
exercises.hint: Hus is an ett-word.
exercises.feedback: Pick the front word that matches the noun.
exercises.explanation: Hus is an ett-word, so the new house is det nya huset.

mistakes.why: Den goes with en-words. Hus is an ett-word.
De is for plurals, and huset is one house.

exercises.instruction: Write the adjective röd in the right form.
exercises.hint: After den the adjective takes one ending for all genders.
exercises.feedback: Adjectives between den and the noun end in -a.
exercises.explanation: After den, det or de the adjective ends in -a: den röda tröjan.

mistakes.why: After den the adjective takes its -a ending.
Rött is for an ett-word without the. Here den and the noun ending call for -a.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.hint: Look at the noun at the end.
exercises.feedback: With den and an adjective, the noun still needs its own ending.
exercises.explanation: Swedish marks the twice: den in front and -en on the noun. The big car is den stora bilen.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the noun is missing its ending.
The adjective must end in -a after den, and that was not the error here.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: The old dog is sleeping. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Hund is an en-word.
exercises.feedback: Pick the front word that matches hund.
exercises.explanation: En hund is an en-word, so the old dog is den gamla hunden.

mistakes.why: Det belongs to ett-words; hund is an en-word.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: The new books are on the shelf.
answers: De nya böckerna står på hyllan.
De nya böckerna ligger på hyllan.
De nya böckerna är på hyllan.
exercises.hint: The plural of bok is böcker.
exercises.feedback: Plural with an adjective: de, adjective -a, noun -na.
exercises.explanation: The new books is de nya böckerna: de for plural, nya, and böcker + na.

answers: Den nya böckerna står på hyllan.
mistakes.why: Den is for one en-word; for plurals the front word is de.

answers: De nya böcker står på hyllan.
mistakes.why: The noun needs its definite ending too: Swedish marks the twice.

alternatives.message: Common in everyday speech. In writing Swedish uses the front word: de nya böckerna.

exercises.instruction: Add the adjective gammal: the old house. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Hus is an ett-word; gammal becomes gamla.
exercises.feedback: An adjective brings a front word with it.
exercises.explanation: Adding an adjective to huset gives det gamla huset: det, the -a form, and the ending on the noun.

mistakes.why: Common in speech, but the written form, which this exercise asks for, puts det in front: det gamla huset.
The noun keeps its ending: Swedish marks the twice.
Den is for en-words; hus is an ett-word.

exercises.instruction: Choose the noun.
exercises.hint: Min already tells you which car.
exercises.feedback: After my, the noun has no ending.
exercises.explanation: After a possessive like min the noun stays in its bare form: min bil.

mistakes.why: With min in front the noun takes no definite ending; min bilen is not Swedish.

exercises.instruction: Choose the noun.
exercises.hint: Annas already says whose house.
exercises.feedback: After a name with -s, the noun has no ending.
exercises.explanation: Annas hus: after a genitive the noun stays bare, just like after min.

mistakes.why: After a genitive like Annas the noun takes no definite ending.

exercises.instruction: Write the word for key.
exercises.hint: Din comes first.
exercises.feedback: After din the noun stays bare.
exercises.explanation: Din already makes the noun definite, so your key is din nyckel.

mistakes.why: After a possessive the noun takes no ending: din nyckeln is wrong.

exercises.instruction: Fix the error.
exercises.hint: Look at the noun after min.
exercises.feedback: A possessive and a definite ending never go together.
exercises.explanation: After min the noun stays bare: min bil.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the noun after min still has its ending.
Mitt is for ett-words. Bil is an en-word, so min was already right.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: My sister's cat is black. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: Systers already says whose cat.
exercises.feedback: After a genitive the noun stays bare.
exercises.explanation: Systers is a genitive, so cat stays bare: min systers katt.

mistakes.why: After the genitive systers the noun takes no definite ending.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: Your car is in the garage.
exercises.hint: Your car: the noun stays bare. The garage: it takes an ending.
exercises.feedback: Only the noun with a possessive stays bare.
exercises.explanation: Din bil has no ending because of din. Garage has no possessive, so the garage is garaget.

mistakes.why: After din the noun takes no ending.
Garage has no possessive, so it still needs its ending to mean the garage.

exercises.instruction: Replace the definite form with min: my house. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Hus is an ett-word, so my is mitt.
exercises.feedback: When the possessive comes, the ending goes.
exercises.explanation: Mitt is the ett form of my, and after it the noun loses its ending: mitt hus.

mistakes.why: After a possessive the noun drops its definite ending.
Min is for en-words; hus needs mitt.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for dogs in general.
exercises.hint: Are you talking about all dogs or particular ones?
exercises.feedback: General statements use the bare plural, as in English.
exercises.explanation: Dogs in general is the bare plural hundar, as English says I like dogs.

mistakes.why: Hundarna means the dogs, particular ones you both know. The sentence is about dogs in general.

exercises.instruction: Choose the word for the dogs.
exercises.hint: Which dogs? The ones in the garden.
exercises.feedback: Particular dogs take the definite ending.
exercises.explanation: These are particular dogs, the ones in the garden, so Swedish says hundarna.

mistakes.why: Hundar means dogs in general; these dogs are pointed out by i trädgården.

exercises.instruction: Write the word for coffee.
exercises.hint: Coffee in general, not a particular cup.
exercises.feedback: Drinks and food in general stay bare.
exercises.explanation: You drink coffee as a habit, so the noun stays bare: kaffe.

mistakes.why: Kaffet means the coffee, a particular coffee. English and Swedish both say coffee here.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.hint: Both nouns are general, as in English.
exercises.feedback: No the in English, no ending in Swedish.
exercises.explanation: This is a general statement, so both nouns stay bare: katter, fisk.

mistakes.why: Those endings mean the cats and the fish, particular ones. The English speaks about cats in general.
Katterna means particular cats; the sentence is about all cats.

exercises.instruction: Translate into Swedish.
exercises.source: The cat is sleeping on the bed.
exercises.hint: A particular cat and a particular bed.
exercises.feedback: English the becomes an ending.
exercises.explanation: Both are known things, so both take the ending: katten, sängen.

mistakes.why: Without endings the nouns lose the meaning the.
The bed is a particular bed too, so säng needs its ending.

exercises.instruction: Make it about the apples you both know: the apples. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.hint: Äpplen ends in -n.
exercises.feedback: Known things take the ending.
exercises.explanation: For particular apples, the plural äpplen takes -a: äpplena.

mistakes.why: That is the original sentence: apples in general.
Äpplet is one apple; the sentence is plural.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: Children love animals. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.hint: A general truth, no the in English.
exercises.feedback: Leave the definite form unused.
exercises.explanation: Children and animals in general are bare: barn, djur.

mistakes.why: Barnen means the children, particular ones. The English is about all children.
